title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Part II of the 'Longue Marche' follow-up, 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. An element of the Teichmüller/GT-type group N_{0,3}^{!~} (for example an actual Galois automorphism) is studied through its image in GL(2,Ẑ). The previous page's remark says the formulas hold in GL(2,Ẑ) once α, β and f are fixed. That image is encoded by three pieces of data:
- α, conjugating the order-3 element ρ (the j=0 inertia);
- β, conjugating σ_∞ (the order-2/order-4 elliptic element, j=1728);
- f, a lift with α_0=f^{-1}α and β_0=f^{-1}β.
These satisfy the loop relation β σ_∞ β^{-1} α ρ α^{-1} = ε l_0^ν. Write α=(a b; c d), β=(r s; t u), δ=det α, μ=δ/(c²+cd+d²), ν=(μ-1)/2.

(84)-(87): replace (α,β,f) by (l_0^n α, l_0^n β, l_0^n f) with n∈Ẑ, where l_0 is upper-triangular unipotent.
- Left multiplication by l_0^n does not change the bottom rows, so c,d,t,u are unchanged.
- α_0=f^{-1}α and β_0=f^{-1}β are unchanged.
- δ is unchanged because det l_0^n=1, hence μ, ε_2 and α_2 (from (79)) are unchanged.
- Therefore the invariant u_{α,β,f} is unchanged; Grothendieck remarks that this is more than is needed.
- The loop relation is also preserved: the left side is conjugated by l_0^n, and the right side ε l_0^ν commutes with l_0^n.

Recalled Proposition (from an earlier page): let μ∈Ẑ*, with signs ε_2≡μ (mod 4) and ε_3≡μ (mod 3), and let c,d,t,u∈Ẑ. There exist a,b,r,s with det α=ε_3, det β=1 and the loop relation α ρ(α)^{-1} = ε_2 (β σ_∞(β^{-1})) l_1^ν (relations (73)) if and only if
(88) ε_3(c²+cd+d²) = ε_2(t²+u²) = 1/μ.
The set of such pairs is a torsor under Ẑ acting by (α,β) ↦ (l_0^n α, l_0^n β).

Modern reading: c²+cd+d² and t²+u² are the norm forms of Z[ω] and Z[i], the CM orders of the elliptic points j=0 and j=1728 of M_{1,1}. So the condition says that the twisted cyclotomic parameter 1/μ is simultaneously a norm from (Ẑ⊗Z[ω])* and from (Ẑ⊗Z[i])*. By local class field theory, the only obstructions are at the ramified primes 3 and 2. These are exactly the sign corrections ε_3 (μ mod 3) and ε_2 (μ mod 4).

The margin NB asks whether, for fixed μ, every (c,d,t,u) satisfying (88) actually occurs. The next page continues this into the 'adelic invariants' Θ=(μ,c,d,t,u) of a GT/Galois element, well defined up to the l_0-torsor.
errors: No mathematical error detected; the invariance claims (85)-(87) check out directly.

The torsor statement needs the same n∈Ẑ on α and β. Bottom-row preservation alone only gives independent unipotent factors; it is the coupling through the loop relation that forces equality. This is left implicit (the next page tags it 'Exercice').
In the next-page transcription, 'ℓ_0^u' should almost certainly read ℓ_0^n, since u is already a matrix entry.

ideas.what: Invariance of the data (c,d,t,u,μ,α_0,β_0, u_{α,β,f}) under simultaneous left multiplication by the unipotent l_0^n
ideas.modern_name: Ambiguity of the conjugating elements by the centralizer of the tangential-base-point inertia

ideas.what: The existence of α,β satisfying the loop relation in GL(2,Ẑ) is equivalent to 1/μ (twisted by ε_3, ε_2) being represented by the Eisenstein norm form c²+cd+d² and the Gaussian norm form t²+u²; solutions form a Ẑ-torsor
ideas.modern_name: Image of the GT/Galois action in the congruence completion SL2(Ẑ)/GL2(Ẑ); norm conditions from the CM orders Z[ω], Z[i] at the elliptic points of M_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in work on Galois action at elliptic points / CM points (e.g. Nakamura, Ihara); unsure of an explicit matching statement

ideas.what: Adelic invariants Θ=(μ,c,d,t,u) attached to an element of N_{0,3}^{!~}, the best invariants available while a,b,r,s have no constructive characterization
ideas.modern_name: Invariants of GT elements modulo the unipotent ambiguity

missed.claim: The GL2(Ẑ)-level loop relation reduces to simultaneous representability of the cyclotomic parameter by the norm forms of the CM orders Z[ω] (j=0) and Z[i] (j=1728). The sign corrections ε_3, ε_2 are exactly the local norm-index obstructions at the ramified primes 3 and 2. This implicitly ties the GT loop equation to CM / local class field theory at the elliptic points of M_{1,1}.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a clean arithmetic criterion for which 'linear parts' of GT elements are compatible with the two elliptic-point relations. It could be compared with the known Galois action on Tate modules of CM curves at j=0 and j=1728.

missed.claim: The margin asks whether, for fixed μ, every (c,d,t,u) satisfying (88) arises. This is a realizability question for the adelic invariants Θ by GT (or by Gal(Q̄/Q)).
missed.quote: NB Pour μ fixé, ... c,d,t,u satisfaisant les relations (88) ... ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete, low-level piece of the question of the image of GT versus Galois. Here it is restricted to the congruence (GL2(Ẑ)) quotient, where it might be decidable.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly bookkeeping: invariance under l_0^n plus a recalled proposition. The recalled criterion, which reads the loop relation as Eisenstein/Gaussian norm conditions with sign corrections at 3 and 2, is a nice explicit unpublished detail. Its content is, however, close to what specialists would derive from the known congruence-quotient action.
transcription_corrections: The header '$\not{3}00$' looks like a page number 300 (or 400) overwritten. The bottom-left '201' is the archive page number.
The first line probably reads 'sur (α,β,f) les changements ...' rather than 'la diagramme'.
The '(cf prop. p. 389)' reference is uncertain from the image; it may be p. 384.
In the loop relation the left side is α ρ(α)^{-1}, with the factor ε_2 on the right; the transcription has this correctly.
